steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Though I sent the both of you off at the selections, things have changed. You two are now the primary candidates for Morgen und Abend.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Things have changed? What do you mean?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The two who were to perform Morgen und Abend cannot attend the concert now, which is why I had you two brought in.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Cannot attend... Did something happen with them?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: They went to a tavern yesterday afternoon to eat and drink their fill.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Normal enough, but something piddling made those two clowns pick a fight.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: So now, the flautist has a fractured arm, and worse still, the cellist somehow fell on his tailbone. He can't even sit, and there he is lying on his bed claiming he can play standing instead. Ridiculous!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You seem shocked.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This is honestly... beyond expectation.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Is it?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: It only took the second day of selections for this to happen, if I'm frank. If this was anything more than a chance bar fight, then you would be the greatest suspect.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Would I?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No—no, no, no, this has less than nothing to do with me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: My desire is to move you through music, not rough up the innocent.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Fine enough for you to say.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: But you have the money to back Kreide. Paying to stir up trouble should be easy enough for you, shouldn't it?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Herr Czerny, I can testify Ebenholz never did anything like that.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You, testify? Did you glue your eyes to him for all of yesterday?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: —I did.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: And why did you do that?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Of course he didn't 'glue his eyes to me,' the two of us were just together, discussing how to change your mind.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Though we never came to any conclusion in the end.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Kreide, is that the truth?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It is.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: For the time being, in the moment being, I'll believe Kreide.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Thank you, Herr Czerny!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Don't start parading.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: All told, you're standing in. You're still some way from what I require.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Especially you, Ebenholz. You're the drag.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'll give you the one day to rehearse. Come back to my home this evening, and I'll cast my eye.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: You will only be chosen if you can meet my minimum standards. Otherwise, I would rather strike Morgen und Abend from the program. Understand?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Yes. You may rest assured.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Also, Kreide, weren't you missing a cello? Take this one with you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Ca... Can I really?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Of course you can.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If you can meet my demands this evening, then this cello will be yours.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: —Thank you, so, so much!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Alright, off you go. I need to sort out my own thoughts as is—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Is that Ursula? Did you forget your key again?

steps.name: Voice Outside the Door
steps.text: Mr. Czerny, I'm an operator from Rhodes Island. You can call me Hibiscus.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hibiscus! Oh, no, did something happen with my grandpa—

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Hello, Mr. Czerny, it's nice to meet you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: My talk with them is done. If you have business, feel free to take them away.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hibiscus, is there anything new with my grandpa's condition?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Relax, it's okay. Your grandpa's gotten treatment already, and he's looking a lot more stable.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Czerny, it's not Kreide. I actually came here looking for you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'm hoping to get some insight into any change in your condition. Would right now be convenient for you?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: What do you want me for?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: There's been quite a few recent Infected cases of abnormal recovery around the Afterglow. I came here to investigate the whole phenomenon.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: On top of that, you're a household name around here, so I was wondering if you had more of a handle on what's going on.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I've been just fine all along, and I can't say I know how anyone else is doing.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But aren't you holding a farewell concert? That usually—

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'm—sorry—but I need quiet. Can I ask you to leave, for now?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Who is it this time?

steps.name: Voice Outside the Door
steps.text: Mein Herr, open her up. I forgot m'dang key.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Kreide, could you go out of your way to open the door again?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That's an awful lot you're carrying, Oma.
Good boy, you go have a seat. I can carry it by m'self.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It's okay, I can bring this into the kitchen for you!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And this is...?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ursula, distant relative of mine. She's cared for me, always.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Well, this is a rare sight, so many people at our home...

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Bowl me over, you're a noble, aren't you? Oh, m'pologies!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hardly. You can simply call me Ebenholz, if you so wish.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Oh, your Lordy sort better not joke around with old codgers like m'self.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's no joke at all. You can just call me Ebenholz.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Honest?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Then if you don't mind me, please.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Hello, Ms. Ursula!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Oof, what's this Sarka—

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Bah, no! Slip of the tongue, Fräulein, I didn't mean that. Don't take it seriously, now!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's okay, Ms. Ursula, I'm used to it.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Oh, no, no, I have to apologize... really, pardon me!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: What do you need Mein Herr for? Concert matters again?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Not in particular. I wanted to ask if there was any change in Mr. Czerny's condition recently.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: You a doctor?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'm an operator from Rhodes Island. You can call me Hibiscus.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: So you and Andante are coworkers?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Andante's a local operator. I'm here at Vyseheim on business from the landship.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: That's a relief, then.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: It's Andante who gives Mein Herr and me our medicine. Lots of folk get prescriptions from Rhodes Island, here in the Afterglow.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Mein Herr, how's the last few days...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Mein Herr, she's a doctor, now, a doctor who cares about your health. This is good for you.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I didn't ask her to come in!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Well, that's silly, now. If you didn't let her in, she wouldn't be in here.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Last year's when he started feeling unwell. No change when spring came this year. Wouldn't be wanting to do any farewell concert otherwise.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: But since yesterday, he's been looking in much better spirits.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Is there anything else as well?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Let me think...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ursula!

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: Alright, alright, m'lips are sealed.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Thank you so much for your help, Ms. Ursula.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If anything's the matter with Mr. Czerny, please give me a shout.

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: No need to tell us. We'd be asking Rhodes Island for a look if something happened, anyway.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Are you done? Are you happy?

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: All done—

steps.name: Ursula
steps.text: —Oh, me and my memory! Said I'd make potato soup and forgot to even buy potatoes... I'll run back to the market now!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Czerny...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: (Eyes practically full of fire)

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: —Ms. Ursula, I'll come with you! I have some questions about cooking I'd like to ask you!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Well, since everyone else has taken their leave, we should also...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Hold it.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Herr Czerny...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The key.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Oma Ursula, your key! Don't forget your key!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Huff, huff...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I never would've imagined an old lady could be so fast. I was a hair from losing her...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I owe it to you for helping me smooth things over back there.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: That's alright, I trust in you. I know you wouldn't do something like that just to be selected.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So, we've handed the key over. Now we should be finding a place in the Afterglow to rehearse.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Can't we just perform right in the street, like everyone does?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: We're rehearsing, not busking. These lanes are too noisy.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: How about your home? Your grandfather just so happens to have vacated, and it wears me to death traveling over from the Cliffy Patio every day.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Could I ask you to lay out a bed for me, and I stay at yours for the next while?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'd welcome you, gladly, but my place is a wreck. I'm scared you wouldn't settle in.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I will, I will. Trust me.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: This is my home.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ergk...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is there something wrong...?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (The room's too small, there's a draft from the window, the timber is molding, there's practically no soundproofing...)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, It's quite fine. Quite fine.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: —Hold on, there's only a single bed here. Where does your grandpa sleep?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: He sleeps in the bed. I sleep here on the floor.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But... isn't this just a rug?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: For a rug, it's pretty nice, and I'm used to sleeping on it by now.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: If you're going to live here, then I'll stay on the floor. It's no problem.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let's just rehearse for now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No good. I'm stuck at this mordent.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It's alright. We can start again from the last bar on the line above.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's this mordent...

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Should I slow down slightly at this part?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No need, it's only an ornament. I'm just being slightly hesitant.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: —This again!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Ebenholz, I'll drop the tempo. Don't put an ornament at the end there, just play through like it's a single note.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The mark is printed on the score!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But you're straining your breath all the way in the bar before, just so you can brace for the mordent.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Wonderful! We played it all the way through!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But I omitted that ornament, and Czerny will hear that, I'm sure of it.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It's alright, we still have time.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Easily said. With the state we're in now, you've no need for further rehearsal. I'm the only one who still has to spend time on this.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: No, don't be like that. I have parts I'm not playing well myself.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Look, here. I didn't express these dynamics at all just now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: And there's a few parts I've been barely forcing through. It's still too early to say I'm fluent.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You gave me a heart attack. I thought you'd already completely mastered this.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Haha. We've had so little time, and it's not like you could really be fluent in a single go. You have to take a lot of things nice and slow.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let's take a break for now, and then we'll work out all the kinks.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: O'er lofty Hills, the Fiend steps into Twilight's Midst agaze.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The Blood hides Plague within, slow beckons Death to creep all Ways.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Pestilence from Shadow wanton spouts, spews Ruin in Prelude.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Fades Finale's Ensemble; Woe deprives of Sun's last Rays.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: What do you think of these edits?
It's more or less the same as the previous edition. You're sure this prophecy will drive out the Rhodes Islander?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: A prophecy alone likely isn't enough, but if we add Their Majesties' names, then use it as a pretext to cause a tiny little uproar... the chance it'll succeed is great, and there won't be any real harm should it fail.
Can you ensure the spread of this prophecy will be confined to the Afterglow?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Please be assured. Previous small-scale disseminations of prophecies have not left any traces of their spread; moreover, as an Infected settlement—
Then do it.
